newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - December 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - December 30.

text.p: The following stories appeared in Monday's edition of Daily Variety:
HOLLYWOOD - Turner and New Line's Michael ascended to the top of the three-day Christmas weekend box office chart with an angelic $17.8 million studio-estimated gross.
WASHINGTON - FCC Commissioner James Quello, who has been a key ally to the broadcasting industry and a thorn in the side of current chairman Reed Hundt, will step down after 23 years with the agency.
NEW YORK - News Corp is planning a public offering for its yet-to-be launched satellite TV business, American Sky Broadcasting.

NEW YORK - Billionaire Ronald Perelman filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection Friday for his Marvel Entertainment Group, cutting off debate with financier Carl Icahn about Perelman's plans for restructuring the struggling company.

HOLLYWOOD - With Oscar competition picking up steam, two things are clear: first, winning a major Academy Award this year should yield a B.O. bonanza, as nearly all the favorites still have abundant playing time ahead of them, Stateside and abroad. Second, the major studios are likely minority participants in the bonanza. Even the most optimistic executives admit that the majors this year have delivered perhaps the weakest lineup of Oscar prospects since the awards began in 1927.
